title: Every Skybase Primitive is wrapped in an identical Hub Document exposing activation status and per-status Instance directories
content:
Each Primitive Instance tree under A.6.1.1.4.2 repeats a fixed five-part Hub Document: a Global Activation Status (`Completed`, `Active`, or `Inactive`), an Active Instances Directory, a Completed Instances Directory, an In Progress Invocations Directory, and a Hub Data Repository. Compare A.6.1.1.4.2.1.1.1 (Agent Creation), A.6.1.1.4.2.1.4.1 (Agent Token) and A.6.1.1.4.2.2.1.1 (Executor Accord) — the headings are interchangeable; only the values differ.

The uniformity is the design. Because state is expressed as *location plus status field* rather than prose, the same question can be asked of any primitive on any Agent: is it switched on, what is running, what finished, what is mid-Invocation. An observer does not need to understand the Executor Accord Primitive to determine that Skybase has one Active Instance of it.

The cost is verbosity — the majority of the Skybase Artifact by volume is this scaffolding, including directories that exist only to state that they are empty. The Atlas pays that cost to get a machine-readable, position-addressable state surface across a heterogeneous set of primitives.

The second-order effect is that primitive *activation* becomes an auditable governance fact rather than an inference from behaviour: turning a capability on requires editing a named status document in the Artifact.
description: Global Activation Status plus Active/Completed/In-Progress directories and a Hub Data Repository give each primitive the same queryable lifecycle surface regardless of what it does.
